name: Placeholder culture, then scRNA-seq
description: SCHEMA EXAMPLE, not a design. Generic workflow that grows cells in their capsules first and then runs the scRNA-seq shape, here so the schema, the planner and the twin have something to chew on. Every reagent, time and temperature is a placeholder. The VOLUMES are not arbitrary: every exchange declares what it is FOR in `exchange_kind` and is sized from that against chip/placeholder_chip_spec.json. There is one `fill` - step 1 loads a dry chamber - and everything after it goes into liquid that is already there, so it is a `sweep`: at least 4.61 chamber volumes in total, which is -ln(1 - 0.99) for the 99% exchange.target_fraction in contracts/parameters.json, because a well-mixed chamber keeps exp(-V) of its old liquid after V chamber volumes. The culture perfusion moves far more than that, and for a perfusion that is correct: it is a continuous feed over 20 minutes, not a single pass. Nothing here is a `partial`. Two different shear bounds apply on this chip and the steps say which: the perfusion puts cells in culture, so it is held to shear.culture_ceiling_dyn_cm2; every other step handles capsules, where the bound is capsule.escape_pressure_kpa across the weir, and 50 uL/min puts about 2.5 kPa across a full capsule bed - half the escape pressure, and inside the 0.7 planning margin. The old 100 uL/min sat exactly ON the escape pressure.

steps.note: Load the capsule suspension into the exchange chamber. One chamber volume: a load FILLS the chamber, so the chamber's own volume (3.638 uL) is the only sensible number. This step used to say 100 uL, 27x what the chamber holds.

Slowly perfuse culture media through the chamber. PERFUSION: 50 uL is 13.7 chamber volumes, well past the 4.61 a single sweep needs, and that is the point of a perfusion rather than an overfill - unlike every other step here the volume is set by the time and the rate. The rate is NOT a free placeholder: this step puts cells in culture in this chamber, so it is the one step on this chip where the 0.01 dyn/cm2 culture shear ceiling applies, and 2.9 uL/min is 85% of the flow that reaches it. The old 10 uL/min was 3x over.
Culture the cells inside their capsules at body temperature.

Rinse the media out three times, immediately before the lyse. SWEEP: 1.54 chamber volumes per wash, 4.62 in total, which is what the 99% exchange goal needs. The reagent is named as a RINSE because that is what it is, and it is the step's purpose that picks its shear ceiling: this chamber has been in culture, but these cells are about to be lysed on purpose, so the bound is shear.prelysis_rinse_ceiling_dyn_cm2 and not the 0.01 culture ceiling. Held to the culture ceiling this rinse would take about 12 minutes and perturb the cells far more than it protects them.

Swap in lysis buffer to open the cells, keeping the capsules on the weir. SWEEP, not a fill: the chamber is full of rinse buffer, so one chamber volume would leave over a third of it behind and dilute the lysis chemistry by the same share. 4.62 chamber volumes in one pass.
Exchange into the RT mix. SWEEP: an enzyme mix has to arrive undiluted, so this clears the lysis buffer rather than topping it up.
Hold warm while the RT mix works.
Split the capsules evenly into the four split chambers.

Give split chamber 1 reagent A. SWEEP of the SPLIT chamber: 4.63 of its 1.273 uL volumes, not of the exchange chamber's. The point of a split is that the four get DIFFERENT reagents, so carryover is what would blur them together.
Give split chamber 2 reagent B. SWEEP: 4.63 split-chamber volumes.
Give split chamber 3 reagent C. SWEEP: 4.63 split-chamber volumes.
Give split chamber 4 reagent D. SWEEP: 4.63 split-chamber volumes.
Pool the capsules back into one chamber.
Wash the pooled capsules three times. SWEEP: 1.55 pool-chamber volumes (2.911 uL each) per wash, 4.64 in total.
Release the library and send it to the outlet. 3.9 pool-chamber volumes, which is -ln(1 - 0.98) for the release.target_fraction goal rather than the exchange one.
